questions.q: What does log shipping actually do, mechanically?
options: Periodically backs up the transaction log on the primary, copies the backup file to a secondary, and restores it there, on a repeating schedule
Continuously streams every transaction to the secondary in real time, like an Availability Group
Takes a full backup of the entire database every few minutes
Replicates only schema changes, never data
questions.explain: Log shipping is backup-copy-restore, repeated on a schedule — not continuous streaming like an AG or geo-replication.

questions.q: Why is log shipping's RPO directly tied to the log-backup job's schedule?
options: Because the secondary can never be more current than the most recently shipped and restored log backup — running that job every 15 minutes means a 15-minute best-case RPO
Because log shipping has no relationship at all to RPO
Because log shipping always achieves zero data loss regardless of schedule
Because the copy job schedule is irrelevant to how current the secondary is
questions.explain: The secondary is only as current as the last backup that was shipped and restored, so the job's interval sets the achievable RPO.

questions.q: Why would a DBA choose log shipping over an Availability Group in a hybrid on-prem-to-Azure scenario?
options: Log shipping doesn't care that the primary and secondary sit in fundamentally different environments, works on Standard Edition, and supports a wider range of SQL Server versions
Log shipping is always faster and has lower RPO than an Availability Group
Availability Groups cannot be used in any hybrid scenario under any circumstances
Log shipping requires Enterprise Edition, just like Availability Groups
questions.explain: Log shipping's simplicity and broad edition/version support make it a fit for hybrid topologies where a full AG may not apply or may be more than needed.

questions.q: What are the three SQL Server Agent jobs that implement log shipping?
options: A backup job on the primary, a copy job that moves the file, and a restore job on the secondary
A full backup job, a differential backup job, and an index rebuild job
A monitoring job, an alerting job, and a notification job
Log shipping does not use SQL Server Agent jobs at all
questions.explain: Log shipping runs as three scheduled jobs: backup (primary), copy (moves the file), and restore (secondary).

questions.q: Why is bringing a log-shipped secondary online a manual recovery step rather than an automatic promotion?
options: Because log shipping is fundamentally backup-copy-restore, not continuous replication with a standing, ready replica — the secondary sits in STANDBY/NORECOVERY until deliberately brought online
Because Microsoft disabled automatic promotion for log shipping as a licensing restriction
Because log-shipped secondaries are never in a recoverable state at all
Because log shipping only works with Azure SQL Database, which has no manual failover option
questions.explain: Since it's backup-copy-restore rather than live replication, recovering a log-shipped secondary is a deliberate, multi-step operation.
